title: unify-credential-modes-and-peekable-stream-iterator-cross-sdk-ergonomic-bump
author: Sofia Chang
release_notes: Introduce CredentialMode enum across Python/TS/Go SDKs, add a peekable streaming iterator to improve ergonomic consumption of chunked responses, harmonize retry/backoff presets, and bump SDK package versions to align with the new session APIs.
description: Context: Multiple SDK consumers requested clearer credential behaviors and a simpler streaming consumer pattern. This PR introduces a small, explicit CredentialMode enum (AUTO|PINNED|DELEGATED) across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, harmonizes default retry/backoff presets to match runtime SLOs, and adds a peekable stream iterator abstraction to make chunk-aware consumers easier to write. Motivation: reduce accidental double-refreshes, improve cross-lang parity for session lifecycle, and reduce user code complexity when implementing lookahead on streaming responses. Summary of changes: - Add CredentialMode contract and adapter in core session layer (sdks/*/session) - Implement CredentialMode-aware credential provider fallback chain with telemetry hooks - Add PeekableStreamIterator (py: IterablePeek, ts: PeekableAsyncIterator, go: PeekableChan) with small memory bounds and deterministic close semantics - Align retry presets and expose an ergonomic RetryProfile builder for advanced use - Add compatibility shim for Node backpressure (ts) preventing unbounded in-memory buffering - Update docs and migration notes and bump package versions (py 2.8.0, ts 1.16.0, go v0.10.0) Checklist: [x] unit tests for credential modes and adapter chains [x] integration tests for stream iterator under chunked responses [x] e2e smoke on hosted API against a Canary model [x] docs: cross-sdk migration guide and examples [x] changelog entries Impact: API surface additions are additive (new enum, new iterator helper). There is a recommended migration for advanced users who previously relied on implicit token refresh side-effects. See release notes for steps.

review_conversation: Priya: Can we avoid shipping both Peekable and the older StreamHelper to prevent confusion? Author: Kept StreamHelper for backwards compatibility but marked deprecated and added a migration note. Liam: The CredentialMode.Auto fallback still triggered two refreshes in a race when the session lease expired; added a token fetch mutex in Go and a guarded promise in TS to serialize refresh. Diego: Request to expose telemetry tag for credential_mode in metrics; added tag and unit tests. Priya: CI flake on the typescript backpressure test; root cause was the Node stream draining order — added a small delay to the test and hardened the shim. Approvals: Priya approved after fixes, Liam approved after addressing double-refresh races, Diego approved with telemetry change.
ci_details: Pipeline: sdk-lint -> unit-tests -> integration-smoke -> crosslang-e2e. Initial run: lint passed, unit-tests failed in ts backpressure test (flaky). Rerun TS unit-tests after shim tweak: pass. Crosslang-e2e run against canary model produced 98% success within latency SLO. Build artifacts: sdks/python/dist/redwood-2.8.0.tar.gz, sdks/typescript/dist/@redwood/sdk-1.16.0.tgz, sdks/go/bin/redwood-sdk-v0.10.0.zip
notes_testing: Unit tests added for edge cases: stale token during long-lived stream, peek after close, concurrent peek+next races. Local fuzzing run (1000 randomized message boundaries) showed stable memory under the configured peek window. Manual verification: python example consumer using IterablePeek consumes first N tokens without needing to buffer the rest; TS sample shows backpressure preserved when piping to a writable stream. Go integration ran on a small Dedicated cluster and showed no deadlocks after the token fetch mutex fix.
merge_outcome: squash-merged by Sofia Chang on 2026-02-02. Commit message summarised key changes; changelog updated. Backported minor docs fix to release/v1 branch in a follow-up PR.
migration_notes: High-level: 1) If you previously relied on implicit refresh side-effects, set CredentialMode=PINNED to preserve behavior or migrate to AUTO with tests. 2) Replace legacy StreamHelper.peek hacks with PeekableStreamIterator for lookahead. 3) Update retry presets only if you used custom backoff - new defaults are safer for low-latency workloads.
notes: This PR focused on ergonomics rather than behaviour changes; customers relying on internal refresh timing should read migration notes. No security-sensitive surface changes were made; audit tracked the new telemetry tag.
